clue.text: Lots of info at short notice sent back to HQ

indicators.note: sent back tells us the words before it are to be read in the opposite direction

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a brief notice
a base is a headquarters

explanation.surface: Information is rushed back to headquarters at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses 'at' plus the short notice to give DATA; 'to' is merely a link word, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A database is an organised store holding a great quantity of information.

clue.text: If you're smart, you'll cut one just a little

definitions.text: If you're smart, you'll cut one

definitions.meaning: a small amount, as of milk

explanation.definitionFit: Dash appears in the idiom 'cut a dash' and also means a small quantity.

clue.text: Artist from a culture involved with tool use

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter emerges from a society that uses tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges A CULTURE with TOOL USE; 'with' joins the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec was a French painter famed for his Moulin Rouge posters.

clue.text: Singer, with a single exception, accepting Italian

indicators.note: accepting means the first piece takes the next one inside it

parts.note: 'bar one' means except for one
It is a common abbreviation for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: A vocalist, unusual in one respect, takes on an Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a single exception' is a roundabout way of saying 'bar one'; 'accepting' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A baritone is a male singer whose voice lies between tenor and bass.

clue.text: Wood formerly used for cooking utensil

definitions.meaning: an old name for a lofted wooden golf club, roughly a three-wood
a kitchen implement for stirring and serving

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the two definitions. 'Wood' is a golf club, not timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoon was an early golf club name, and a spoon is also an everyday kitchen implement.

clue.text: Crazy villain finally caught by copper, say

indicators.note: caught by means the next item holds the earlier piece inside it

parts.note: copper is an example of a metal, hence 'say'

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word villain

explanation.surface: A villain ends up arrested by a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal; N from 'villain finally' sits inside METAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental is informal British slang for mad or crazy.

clue.text: Crude shelter for animal at close of day

parts.note: an earth is the burrow of a fox or badger

indicators.note: close of picks out the final letter of the word day

explanation.surface: A rough shelter for a beast at nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is positional: Y follows EARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy describes humour that is coarse or crude.

clue.text: A little artistic work that could make this blanket much different

indicators.note: much different means the letters are made very different by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A small drawing could transform a blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges THIS BLANKET MUCH; 'that could make' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail sketch is a quick small drawing, or a brief description.

clue.text: In a way, ready to get one run for county

indicators.note: In places the following pieces inside the stated way

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road, a way
ready, or readies, is slang for cash
I is the Roman numeral for one
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Somewhere on the road, getting enough cash for a run to a county.
explanation.walkthrough: CASH + I + R go In LANE; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is a county in north-west England.

clue.text: About a series of lessons, naturally

parts.note: of can mean about, as in 'speak of'
a course is a programme of classes

explanation.surface: Regarding a set of classes, it goes without saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Of course and naturally are interchangeable exclamations of obviousness.

clue.text: Honest start to prepare for fight

parts.note: square means fair and honest, as in a square deal
the off is the start of a race

explanation.surface: Someone honestly begins getting ready for a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To square off is to adopt a fighting stance facing an opponent.

clue.text: Profligate knight in French city

parts.note: a roué is a dissolute, profligate man
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A dissolute knight lives in a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouen is the Norman city on the Seine where Joan of Arc died.

clue.text: Type choice of characters frequently used in statistics

definitions.meaning: a type is a kind or class of thing

definitions.text: choice of characters frequently used in statistics
definitions.meaning: ordering records by a chosen field of characters or numbers is a routine operation in data handling and statistics

explanation.walkthrough: A double definition: a kind of thing, and the operation of putting data into order.
explanation.definitionFit: Sort is both a noun for a kind and a verb for arranging data in order.

clue.text: Nothing can cause this fearful condition for long

definitions.text: Nothing can cause this fearful condition for long

parts.words: Nothing can cause this fearful condition for long
parts.note: read 'Nothing' as 'no thing that is new': a dread of novelty, which by definition cannot last since the new soon becomes familiar

explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic definition: the condition is a fear of anything new, and nothing stays new for long.
explanation.definitionFit: Neophobia is the medical term for an abnormal dread of novelty or anything unfamiliar.

clue.text: An attractive fish? That can't be right — it's smaller

parts.note: taken as written
cute means attractive

indicators.note: can't be says the named letter must be taken away

parts.note: the angler is a fish, the anglerfish

explanation.surface: Spotting a pretty fish, someone doubts it, saying it is smaller than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That can't be right' drops R from ANGLER; an acute angle is smaller than a right angle, which gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute angle is one less than ninety degrees, so smaller than a right angle.

clue.text: Mob involved in arson act so

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Gangsters are caught up in an arson attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' rearranges ARSON ACT SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosa Nostra is the American Mafia, the archetypal criminal mob.

clue.text: Without it being raised, pays out fixed wages

indicators.note: Without in the old sense of outside: the pays-out word goes round the other

parts.note: spends means pays out

indicators.note: in a down clue, being raised turns the word upwards, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: Without it rising, someone pays out regular salaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense 'outside'; in a down clue 'being raised' turns 'it' upwards to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Stipends are fixed regular payments, as to clergy.

clue.text: Composer dear to the Welsh

definitions.meaning: Johann Sebastian, the German Baroque composer
in Welsh, ... is an affectionate form of address, like 'dear' or 'love'

explanation.surface: A composer is cherished in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Bach is the German composer; it is also Welsh for little one, used as an endearment.

clue.text: Get nothing out of play, initially one certain to fold

indicators.note: initially says the out-of-play piece comes first in the answer

parts.note: a dead ball is out of play
in cricket a duck is a score of nothing

explanation.surface: A gambler wins nothing from a game and is bound to fold.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a batsman's score of zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead duck is a plan or venture certain to fail.

clue.text: Cost of ring

definitions.meaning: a charge paid to use a road or bridge
to sound a bell slowly, as for a funeral

explanation.definitionFit: A toll is a fee for passage; to toll is to ring a bell with slow strokes.

clue.text: Graves, etc, found here in underground chamber

definitions.meaning: Graves is a Bordeaux wine; bottles of it are stored in such a place
a cellar is an underground room

explanation.walkthrough: 'Graves' suggests burial places, fitting an underground chamber, but it is the Bordeaux wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine cellar is a basement room where bottles such as Graves are kept.

clue.text: Be economical with fabric increased by penny

parts.note: scrim is a light open-weave cotton fabric

explanation.surface: Save money on material that went up by a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'increased by' adds P after SCRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to be thrifty and save money.

clue.text: Fit mouthpiece for a Shakespearean role

parts.note: an ague is a fit of fever and shivering
cheek, insolent talk, is mouth

explanation.surface: A bout of fever affects an actor's mouthpiece in a Shakespeare part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word. Sir Andrew Aguecheek is the foolish knight in Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Andrew Aguecheek is a comic character in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Novelist's parrot swallowing folio

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: swallowing means the bird takes the next piece inside

parts.note: the kaka is a New Zealand parrot

explanation.surface: A writer's pet bird gulps down a page.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Kafka was the Prague-born novelist who wrote The Trial.

clue.text: Nobleman in this country absorbed into lower classes

indicators.note: absorbed into means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification
for a British newspaper, this country is the UK

explanation.surface: An aristocrat in Britain is assimilated into the working class.
explanation.walkthrough: British market research grades the population A, B, C1, C2, D, E, so the lower classes are D and E; UK goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is the highest rank of the British peerage below royalty.

clue.text: Soldier captured crossing river in front of boat

indicators.note: crossing here means the captured soldier straddles the river letter

parts.note: a POW is a prisoner of war

explanation.surface: A prisoner crosses a river at the bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The prow is the forward-most part of a ship's bow.

clue.text: Writer using extract from Browning or Kipling

indicators.note: extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An author quotes a passage by one of two English poets.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownin-G OR KI-pling. Maxim Gorki (or Gorky) was a Russian writer; 'using' is part of the definition, read as 'writer employing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxim Gorki was a Russian novelist and playwright, the author of The Lower Depths.

clue.text: Person avoiding court action, more skilful hiding gold left

indicators.note: hiding means the first piece conceals the following ones within it

parts.note: defter means more dexterous or skilful
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A dodger of the courts, cleverer than most, has stashed some bullion.
explanation.definitionFit: A defaulter fails to meet an obligation such as appearing in court or paying a debt.

clue.text: Save king from part of work

indicators.note: from here signals the king is taken away from the next piece

parts.note: an excerpt is a passage taken from a longer work
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is rescued from part of a literary work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like a rescue verb but means 'but' or 'apart from'; R removed from EXCERPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Save, as a preposition meaning 'apart from', is a synonym of except.

clue.text: Silly walk host presented for TV programme

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters behave foolishly and are jumbled

explanation.surface: A presenter with a silly walk fronts a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' rearranges WALK HOST; 'presented for' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A talk show is a television programme of chat between a host and guests.
